mechanics.name: Windows of Opportunity
mechanics.currentEffect: Reveals the Auras of Breakable Walls, Pallets, and Windows within 24/28/32 m.
activation: A Breakable Wall, Pallet, or Window must be within 24/28/32 metres.
There is no cooldown or manual activation on the current live version.
mechanics.patchNote: Current live effect is the always-on 24/28/32 m aura reveal for Breakable Walls, Pallets, and Windows. 10.2 PTB proposes a window-only rework with 10% faster vaulting and a 40/35/30-second cooldown after vaulting; not live.

editorial.summary: Continuously reveals nearby pallets, windows, and breakable walls so you can route chases around the resources that actually exist.
useCases: See whether a pallet has already been spent before committing to that tile.
Chain one safe resource into the next during chase.
Learn unfamiliar maps and procedural pallet spawns much faster.
counters: The perk gives information, not automatic pathing or loop execution.
Experienced players who already track map RNG and used pallets gain less marginal value.
Aura-reading denial can temporarily remove the information advantage.
pros: Always-on information with no activation condition or cooldown.
Especially valuable in Solo Q where teammates cannot reliably call which pallets they used.
Useful from beginner level all the way through experienced chase play.
cons: Does not directly create speed, Endurance, healing, or generator progress.
Can encourage resource-to-resource running without teaching why a tile is safe if used passively.
Its identity would change substantially under the current 10.2 PTB proposal.
analysis: Windows of Opportunity earns this spot through consistency rather than explosive power. Pallets are consumable resources, and the cost of discovering mid-chase that a pallet is already gone can be an immediate health state. Windows removes that uncertainty while also showing nearby vaults and breakable walls.

For a rusty or newer Survivor it is one of the fastest ways to rebuild map knowledge. More importantly, it does not become useless once you improve. Experienced players still benefit from seeing procedural pallet spawns and from knowing exactly which resources random teammates consumed while they were elsewhere on the map.

The reason we stop at A tier instead of treating it like Will to Live or Unbreakable is that Windows does not itself win the chase. It gives you a better decision tree, but you still need pathing, camera control, loop knowledge, and pallet discipline to convert that information into time. In a coordinated SWF, teammate callouts also reduce some of the information advantage.

The 10.2 PTB would fundamentally split its current identity: Windows would become window-only aura information with a vault-speed effect and cooldown, while Five Moves Ahead would specialize more heavily in pallets. Because that proposal is not live, #8 is based entirely on the current always-on 24/28/32 metre resource-reading version.
editorial.verdict: A-tier overall and one of the best practical perks for a returning player. You already have Kate P1, so this is immediately available and deserves heavy use while rebuilding chase/map knowledge.
